newsitem.title: UK: British farmers take measures to conserve water.
newsitem.headline: British farmers take measures to conserve water.

text.p: Many farmers in Britain are taking early action to conserve water in case the current dry weather continues.

National Farmers Union (NFU) Deputy President Tony Pexton said "Although we are not yet in a serious situation across England and Wales, numerous farmers are doing their part to conserve water to make it go further,"

Farmers have been constructing farm reservoirs, irrigating during early morning and evening to cut evaporation levels, more efficient guaging of the exact water needs of crops, voluntary restrictions, and strict maintenance of irrigation systems.
"By adopting respsonsible practices now, farmers can, and are, working to avoid the need for severe restrictions later in the year," Pexton said.
Although reservoirs in most areas are full, underground water levels in many parts of the U.K. are low.
The South-East and East Anglia, particularly, rely heavily on underground supplies and concern exists among some farmers in these areas about future supplies for irrigation.
Britain's dry summers in 1995 and 1996 saw restrictions placed on irrigating crops which focused farmers' attention on the importance of forward planning.
It is too early to tell whether we will face a drought this summer, but farmers are already making every drop count," the NFUs Pexton said.
